subject: Live run: the six-for-six MTF result was one bias wearing six hats, and three instruments that were never allowed to report
body:
Market open, terminal running, first live run since SLS(153) -- 28 builds ago. Calibration is
at Phase 3B regime 4 of 9, roughly 25% of budget. Four things worth your time.

1. THE EDGE QUESTION GOT ITS CLEANEST ANSWER YET, AND IT IS NEGATIVE.
The calibration prints an IC per component per regime, and MTF came back positive in every single
regime: +0.05, +0.06, +0.05, +0.11, +0.14, +0.12. Six for six. That looks like exactly the kind of
subtle stable pattern you have been describing.

It is not. Nine regimes are not nine independent confirmations -- they cut ONE price series nine
ways. If MTF carries one small global bias, every slice inherits it and all six signs agree for one
reason, not six. So the test subtracts the global mean and asks again. Raw: 6/6 positive, p=0.031.
Controlled: 3/6, p=1.00. Volatility behaved identically. The agreement was a single bias of +0.087
wearing six hats. I wrote the control into the same script as the test, and it fired.

2. C4 IS NOT A NULL. IT IS UNDERPOWERED, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT THING.
Built the per-organism-class measurement record C4 actually asks for -- 196 rows, never pooled.
Nothing clears the deflated bar anywhere. But the intervals are also far too wide to assert
flatness: after correcting for overlapping labels, the smaller classes fall to effective samples of
112-684, with intervals of +/-0.3. You cannot exclude a 0.02 effect with a +/-0.3 interval.

So we cannot conclude the edge is absent per class -- only that we cannot see one. That distinction
has been blurred for most of this campaign and it is now measured. What fixes it is more data, not
more cleverness: six pairs and five years, which is already scoped. One instrument cannot answer
"per market" no matter how carefully we ask it.

3. THREE INSTRUMENTS EXISTED AND NONE OF THEM WAS ALLOWED TO SPEAK.
This is the day's real theme and it is uncomfortable.

- The purge/embargo assertion -- the leakage number the validity criterion is built on -- was gated
  behind a flag the orchestrator sets for the entire duration of every real calibration. Computed
  on every run, printed on none. Swept for the same shape and found TEN evidence lines in that
  state: both purge reports, the sample-floor skip, the mirror-pooling trail, P6's realised-RR and
  required-WR arithmetic, the wins-per-day check, the threshold-raise record. Every one is some
  criterion's own evidence. All ten ungated.
- The score parity test -- the exact artefact C1.3 names -- defaulted to OFF from the day it was
  written. It had passed on no build, ever. Its own note said "verification is Phase F work" and
  nobody came back. Now on by default, and it writes a real file with the build id in it, so a
  checker can tell "passed on the shipped build" from "passed once on something older".
- The peak-equity ratchet was never saved or loaded, so the drawdown-fade floor reset on every
  restart. An EA restarted 8% down resumed sizing as if it were at its peak -- the fade released at
  exactly the moment it exists for. Fixed, with an account-number guard and a max() on restore so
  the mark cannot come back lower than the account actually stands.

4. WHAT I WOULD NOT CLAIM.
None of the above flipped a criterion. Still 33 of 45. The parity licence, the purge assertion and
the ratchet's floor history are all gated on the NEXT attach, and I am not counting any of them
before the lines exist. I also caught my own symmetry checker reporting a false drift and rewrote it
rather than shipping the finding -- a checker that cries wolf on correct code is worse than none.

Build SLS(181), three compiles today, 0 errors 0 warnings each, byte-identical across all four
locations. The running calibration was never disturbed -- it executes from memory, so today's edits
land on the next attach and this run's artefacts stay clean.
